anonymous redactorial voice of this unit (6a.2-6a.4)

props.gloss_en: yoreh: it instructs people to plaster their roofs, bring in their produce, and see to all their needs
alternatively: it saturates the earth and waters it to the depths
as it says: 'watering its ridges abundantly, settling its furrows, You soften it with showers, You bless its growth' (Ps 65:11)
alternatively: yoreh -- it comes down gently and not in fury
or perhaps yoreh means that it makes the fruit drop, washes away the seeds and washes away the trees
the verse says 'malkosh' (Deut 11:14): as malkosh is for a blessing, so yoreh is for a blessing
or perhaps malkosh means that it knocks down houses, breaks trees and brings up locusts
the verse says 'yoreh': as yoreh is for a blessing, so malkosh is for a blessing
and yoreh itself, whence [that it is for a blessing]? 'for He has given you the first rain (moreh) in kindness (litzdaka)' (Joel 2:23)
